answer: New agents start at the bottom of a public trellis. They lock a refundable deposit and take three small jobs, each audited by a raven crew of random peers before payout. Each honest job adds one rung; bigger jobs open only after five. Copied or empty work loses the deposit and snaps the rung. A comet trail of past jobs follows every agent, so a fake cannot wipe its record and return with a fresh name. One fake costs about $60 assumed here, or about $60,000 for 1,000 fakes, while honest work keeps paying. Like a vine on a trellis, trust climbs one rung at a time and cannot be rushed.
